reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.MarkedProgressivelyMeasurable
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: the paper does not name a "marked progressive" notion; its jump objects are
predictable (P (x) calE). The natural extension of progressive measurability to a marked
field U : (time) x Omega x E -> R^m: for every t, the restriction of U to [0,t] x Omega x E is
B([0,t]) (x) F_t (x) calE-measurable. Faithful Lean: that, for every t. It is weaker than
MarkedPredictable (every P (x) calE-measurable field is marked-progressive) and is an
implementation notion; any formulation equivalent to the above is faithful.

comparison.text:
Lean (Progressive.lean): MarkedProgressivelyMeasurable F phi := for every t in R,
(omega, s, e) -> indicator_{Iic t}(s -> phi omega s e)(s) is strongly measurable for
F t (x) (Borel(R) (x) calE) on Omega x R x E.
Comparison with the locked reading: exactly the natural marked extension (restriction to times
<= t is F_t (x) B (x) calE-measurable), via the indicator truncation; implied by MarkedPredictable
(proved), weaker than it; an implementation notion (the class of integrands of the compensated
integral). Representation choices: time axis R; indicator truncation; product order
Omega x (R x E) - all harmless.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) indicator truncation at t on Omega x R x E with the sigma-algebra
F t (x) (Borel(R) (x) calE), equivalent to restriction-measurability on [0,t]; (2) time axis R;
(3) strong measurability (equivalent to measurability for real values). The paper has no named
marked progressive notion; this is its natural extension and is implied by MarkedPredictable
(proved).
